items.name: Ollama + Open WebUI
items.description: Ollama local LLM runtime with Open WebUI, a ChatGPT-style browser interface for chatting with local models.

source.name: Open WebUI official documentation (Docker Compose with Ollama)

items.notes: No models are pulled automatically (they can be multiple GB). Open WebUI's first visitor becomes the local admin account — create it on first load. Pull a model from inside the container with `docker exec <ollama container> ollama pull llama3.2`, or from the Open WebUI Settings > Models screen.
items.compose:
# Adapted from Open WebUI's official Docker Compose example (MIT)
# https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui
services:
  ollama:
    image: docker.io/ollama/ollama:0.12.5
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${OLLAMA_PORT}:11434"
    volumes:
      - ollama-data:/root/.ollama
    healthcheck:
      # The ollama image has no curl/wget; `ollama list` talks to the local API over its own
      # client, so it doubles as a readiness probe.
      test: ["CMD", "ollama", "list"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

  open-webui:
    image: ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:v0.11.4
    depends_on:
      ollama:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      - OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama:11434
      - WEBUI_AUTH=true
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${OPEN_WEBUI_PORT}:8080"
    volumes:
      - open-webui-data:/app/backend/data

volumes:
  ollama-data:
  open-webui-data:

items.name: Keycloak + PostgreSQL
items.description: Keycloak identity and access management backed by PostgreSQL, for local OIDC/SAML development.
items.notes: Runs in `start-dev` mode (HTTP allowed, no TLS) — for local development only. Data is persisted in the PostgreSQL volume.
items.compose:
# Adapted from the official Keycloak documentation's Docker Compose example (Apache-2.0)
# https://www.keycloak.org/server/containers
services:
  postgres:
    image: docker.io/library/postgres:17.6-alpine
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=keycloak
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${PG_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_DB=keycloak
    volumes:
      - keycloak-pg-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U keycloak -d keycloak"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

  keycloak:
    image: quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.7.4
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      - KEYCLOAK_ADMIN=${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN}
      - KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      - KC_DB=postgres
      - KC_DB_URL=jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/keycloak
      - KC_DB_USERNAME=keycloak
      - KC_DB_PASSWORD=${PG_PASSWORD}
      - KC_HEALTH_ENABLED=true
      - KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT=false
    command: ["start-dev"]
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${KEYCLOAK_PORT}:8080"
    healthcheck:
      # The Keycloak image has no curl/wget; /bin/sh is bash, so use its /dev/tcp support to probe
      # the management interface's health endpoint (port 9000) directly.
      test:
        [
          "CMD-SHELL",
          "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/9000 && printf 'GET /health/ready HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n' >&3 && grep -q '\"status\": \"UP\"' <&3"
        ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30

volumes:
  keycloak-pg-data:

items.name: Vault (dev mode)
items.description: HashiCorp Vault in dev server mode: in-memory, auto-unsealed, for local secrets-management experiments.

source.name: HashiCorp Vault official Docker image documentation
source.license: Business Source License 1.1 (Vault server); documentation used under fair use

items.notes: Dev mode: unsealed automatically, all data is in memory and lost on restart, TLS is disabled. Never use dev mode for anything beyond local experimentation. Sign in to the UI with the root token as the password (method: Token).
items.compose:
# Adapted from the official HashiCorp Vault Docker image documentation
# https://hub.docker.com/r/hashicorp/vault
services:
  vault:
    image: docker.io/hashicorp/vault:1.21.1
    cap_add:
      - IPC_LOCK
    environment:
      - VAULT_DEV_ROOT_TOKEN_ID=${VAULT_TOKEN}
      - VAULT_DEV_LISTEN_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0:8200
      - VAULT_ADDR=http://127.0.0.1:8200
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${VAULT_PORT}:8200"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "vault", "status"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

items.name: MongoDB + Mongo Express
items.description: MongoDB database with Mongo Express, a web-based admin UI for browsing collections and documents.
items.notes: Mongo Express is protected by HTTP basic auth using MONGO_EXPRESS_USER/PASSWORD, separate from the MongoDB credentials.
items.compose:
# Adapted from docker/awesome-compose (CC0-1.0) patterns using the official mongo + mongo-express images.
# https://github.com/docker/awesome-compose
services:
  mongo:
    image: docker.io/library/mongo:8.2.1
    environment:
      - MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME=${MONGO_USER}
      - MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD=${MONGO_PASSWORD}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${MONGO_PORT}:27017"
    volumes:
      - mongo-data:/data/db
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "mongosh", "--quiet", "--eval", "db.adminCommand('ping')"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30

  mongo-express:
    image: docker.io/library/mongo-express:1.0.2-20-alpine3.19
    depends_on:
      mongo:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      - ME_CONFIG_MONGODB_ADMINUSERNAME=${MONGO_USER}
      - ME_CONFIG_MONGODB_ADMINPASSWORD=${MONGO_PASSWORD}
      - ME_CONFIG_MONGODB_SERVER=mongo
      - ME_CONFIG_BASICAUTH_USERNAME=${MONGO_EXPRESS_USER}
      - ME_CONFIG_BASICAUTH_PASSWORD=${MONGO_EXPRESS_PASSWORD}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${MONGO_EXPRESS_PORT}:8081"

volumes:
  mongo-data:

items.name: MySQL + Adminer
items.description: MySQL database with Adminer, a lightweight single-file database admin UI, in your browser.
items.notes: In Adminer, set System to MySQL and Server to `mysql` (the in-network hostname) to connect.
items.compose:
# Adapted from docker/awesome-compose (CC0-1.0) patterns using the official mysql and adminer images.
# https://github.com/docker/awesome-compose
services:
  mysql:
    image: docker.io/library/mysql:9.4
    environment:
      - MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=${MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD}
      - MYSQL_USER=${MYSQL_USER}
      - MYSQL_PASSWORD=${MYSQL_PASSWORD}
      - MYSQL_DATABASE=${MYSQL_DATABASE}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${MYSQL_PORT}:3306"
    volumes:
      - mysql-data:/var/lib/mysql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "mysqladmin", "ping", "-h", "localhost", "-u", "root", "-p${MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30

  adminer:
    image: docker.io/library/adminer:5.4.1
    depends_on:
      mysql:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      - ADMINER_DEFAULT_SERVER=mysql
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${ADMINER_PORT}:8080"

volumes:
  mysql-data:

items.name: PostgreSQL + pgAdmin
items.description: PostgreSQL database with pgAdmin 4 for browsing, querying and administering it from a browser.
items.notes: In pgAdmin, add a server with host `postgres`, port 5432 (the in-network port, not PG_PORT) to connect without leaving the browser.
items.compose:
# Adapted from docker/awesome-compose (CC0-1.0) — postgresql-pgadmin sample
# https://github.com/docker/awesome-compose/tree/main/postgresql-pgadmin
services:
  postgres:
    image: docker.io/library/postgres:17.6-alpine
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=${PG_USER}
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${PG_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_DB=${PG_DB}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${PG_PORT}:5432"
    volumes:
      - pg-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${PG_USER} -d ${PG_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

  pgadmin:
    image: docker.io/dpage/pgadmin4:9.7
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      - PGADMIN_DEFAULT_EMAIL=${PGADMIN_EMAIL}
      - PGADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD=${PGADMIN_PASSWORD}
      - PGADMIN_CONFIG_SERVER_MODE=False
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${PGADMIN_PORT}:80"
    volumes:
      - pgadmin-data:/var/lib/pgadmin

volumes:
  pg-data:
  pgadmin-data:

items.name: Redis + RedisInsight
items.description: Redis in-memory data store with RedisInsight for browsing keys, running commands and monitoring.
items.notes: RedisInsight has no login by default; add a database with host `redis`, port 6379 and the generated password to connect.
items.compose:
# Adapted from docker/awesome-compose (CC0-1.0) patterns using the official redis + redisinsight images.
# https://github.com/docker/awesome-compose
services:
  redis:
    image: docker.io/library/redis:8.2.2-alpine
    command: ["redis-server", "--requirepass", "${REDIS_PASSWORD}"]
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${REDIS_PORT}:6379"
    volumes:
      - redis-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "redis-cli -a ${REDIS_PASSWORD} ping | grep -q PONG"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

  redisinsight:
    image: docker.io/redis/redisinsight:2.62
    depends_on:
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${REDISINSIGHT_PORT}:5540"
    volumes:
      - redisinsight-data:/data

volumes:
  redis-data:
  redisinsight-data:

items.name: Mailpit
items.description: SMTP test server that catches outgoing mail and shows it in a web UI — no real emails are sent.
items.notes: Point any app's SMTP settings at localhost:${MAILPIT_SMTP_PORT} with no auth and no TLS; every message shows up in the web UI.
items.compose:
# Adapted from the official Mailpit documentation (MIT)
# https://github.com/axllent/mailpit
services:
  mailpit:
    image: docker.io/axllent/mailpit:v1.31.3
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${MAILPIT_SMTP_PORT}:1025"
      - "127.0.0.1:${MAILPIT_UI_PORT}:8025"
    volumes:
      - mailpit-data:/data
    environment:
      - MP_MAX_MESSAGES=5000
      - MP_DATABASE=/data/mailpit.db
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://localhost:8025/readyz"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

volumes:
  mailpit-data:

items.name: n8n
items.description: n8n workflow automation platform for building integrations and automations with a visual editor.

source.name: n8n official Docker documentation
source.license: Sustainable Use License (n8n server); documentation used under fair use

items.notes: Uses n8n's built-in basic auth for a single local user. Workflow data is stored in SQLite in a named volume.
items.compose:
# Adapted from the official n8n Docker documentation
# https://docs.n8n.io/hosting/installation/docker/
services:
  n8n:
    image: docker.io/n8nio/n8n:1.115.2
    environment:
      - N8N_BASIC_AUTH_ACTIVE=true
      - N8N_BASIC_AUTH_USER=${N8N_USER}
      - N8N_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD=${N8N_PASSWORD}
      - N8N_PORT=5678
      - N8N_PROTOCOL=http
      - N8N_HOST=localhost
      - N8N_EDITOR_BASE_URL=http://localhost:${N8N_PORT}
      - WEBHOOK_URL=http://localhost:${N8N_PORT}/
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${N8N_PORT}:5678"
    volumes:
      - n8n-data:/home/node/.n8n
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:5678/healthz >/dev/null 2>&1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

volumes:
  n8n-data:

items.name: Kafka + Kafka UI
items.description: Single-node Apache Kafka (KRaft mode, no ZooKeeper) with Kafka UI for browsing topics, messages and consumer groups.

source.name: Apache Kafka official image docs + kafbat/kafka-ui (maintained fork of provectus/kafka-ui)

items.notes: Single broker, no authentication — for local development only. The advertised listener is set to localhost:${KAFKA_PORT} so clients on the Mac host connect directly at 127.0.0.1:${KAFKA_PORT}; clients inside the compose network use kafka:29092.
items.compose:
# Adapted from the official apache/kafka image documentation (Apache-2.0, KRaft single-node quickstart:
# https://kafka.apache.org/documentation/#quickstart) and kafbat/kafka-ui's own docker-compose examples
# (Apache-2.0, https://github.com/kafbat/kafka-ui).
#
# Two listeners: PLAINTEXT (in-network, used by kafka-ui and other containers) and EXTERNAL
# (advertised as localhost:${KAFKA_PORT} so the Mac host can connect at 127.0.0.1:${KAFKA_PORT}).
services:
  kafka:
    image: docker.io/apache/kafka:3.9.1
    environment:
      - KAFKA_NODE_ID=1
      - KAFKA_PROCESS_ROLES=broker,controller
      - KAFKA_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://0.0.0.0:29092,CONTROLLER://0.0.0.0:29093,EXTERNAL://0.0.0.0:9092
      - KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://kafka:29092,EXTERNAL://localhost:${KAFKA_PORT}
      - KAFKA_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP=CONTROLLER:PLAINTEXT,PLAINTEXT:PLAINTEXT,EXTERNAL:PLAINTEXT
      - KAFKA_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES=CONTROLLER
      - KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=1@kafka:29093
      - KAFKA_INTER_BROKER_LISTENER_NAME=PLAINTEXT
      - KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_REPLICATION_FACTOR=1
      - KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_REPLICATION_FACTOR=1
      - KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_MIN_ISR=1
      - KAFKA_GROUP_INITIAL_REBALANCE_DELAY_MS=0
      - CLUSTER_ID=ciWo7IWazngRchmPES6q5A==
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${KAFKA_PORT}:9092"
    volumes:
      - kafka-data:/var/lib/kafka/data
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD-SHELL",
          "/opt/kafka/bin/kafka-broker-api-versions.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:29092 >/dev/null 2>&1"
        ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 20

  kafka-ui:
    image: docker.io/kafbat/kafka-ui:v1.5.0
    depends_on:
      kafka:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      - KAFKA_CLUSTERS_0_NAME=local
      - KAFKA_CLUSTERS_0_BOOTSTRAPSERVERS=kafka:29092
      - DYNAMIC_CONFIG_ENABLED=true
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${KAFKA_UI_PORT}:8080"

volumes:
  kafka-data:

items.name: RabbitMQ
items.description: RabbitMQ message broker with the management plugin enabled for browsing queues, exchanges and connections.
items.compose:
# Adapted from the official RabbitMQ Docker image documentation (MIT)
# https://github.com/docker-library/docs/tree/master/rabbitmq
services:
  rabbitmq:
    image: docker.io/library/rabbitmq:4.1.4-management-alpine

items.name: Grafana + Prometheus
items.description: Prometheus metrics server pre-wired as a Grafana data source, for building dashboards over scraped metrics.
items.notes: Prometheus is configured to scrape itself only; the Prometheus data source is pre-provisioned in Grafana at http://prometheus:9090.
items.compose:
# Adapted from docker/awesome-compose (CC0-1.0) — prometheus-grafana sample
# https://github.com/docker/awesome-compose/tree/main/prometheus-grafana
#
# No bind mounts are used (named volumes only), so a one-shot init container writes the
# Prometheus scrape config and the Grafana datasource provisioning file into named volumes
# before the real services start.
services:
  prometheus-config:
    image: docker.io/library/alpine:3.21
    restart: "no"
    volumes:
      - prometheus-config:/config
    entrypoint:
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        cat > /config/prometheus.yml <<'EOF'
        global:
          scrape_interval: 15s
        scrape_configs:
          - job_name: prometheus
            static_configs:
              - targets: ["localhost:9090"]
        EOF

  grafana-provisioning:
    image: docker.io/library/alpine:3.21
    restart: "no"
    volumes:
      - grafana-provisioning:/config
    entrypoint:
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        mkdir -p /config/datasources
        cat > /config/datasources/prometheus.yml <<'EOF'
        apiVersion: 1
        datasources:
          - name: Prometheus
            type: prometheus
            access: proxy
            url: http://prometheus:9090
            isDefault: true
        EOF

  prometheus:
    image: docker.io/prom/prometheus:v3.15.0
    depends_on:
      prometheus-config:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    volumes:
      - prometheus-config:/etc/prometheus
      - prometheus-data:/prometheus
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${PROMETHEUS_PORT}:9090"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9090/-/ready >/dev/null 2>&1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

  grafana:
    image: docker.io/grafana/grafana:13.2.2
    depends_on:
      grafana-provisioning:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      prometheus:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=admin
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - grafana-provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning
      - grafana-data:/var/lib/grafana
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${GRAFANA_PORT}:3000"

volumes:
  prometheus-config:
  prometheus-data:
  grafana-provisioning:
  grafana-data:

items.name: Jaeger
items.description: All-in-one Jaeger for distributed tracing: collector, query UI and in-memory storage in a single container.
items.notes: Traces are stored in memory and lost on restart — for local development only. Point your app's OpenTelemetry exporter at the OTLP endpoint.
items.compose:
# Adapted from the official Jaeger all-in-one Docker quickstart (Apache-2.0)
# https://www.jaegertracing.io/docs/latest/getting-started/
services:
  jaeger:
    image: docker.io/jaegertracing/jaeger:2.21.0
    environment:
      - COLLECTOR_OTLP_ENABLED=true
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${JAEGER_UI_PORT}:16686"
      - "127.0.0.1:${JAEGER_OTLP_GRPC_PORT}:4317"
      - "127.0.0.1:${JAEGER_OTLP_HTTP_PORT}:4318"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:16686 >/dev/null 2>&1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

items.name: Loki + Grafana
items.description: Grafana Loki log aggregation, pre-wired as a Grafana data source for exploring logs.

source.name: Grafana Loki official documentation (docker-compose quickstart pattern)
source.license: Apache-2.0 (documentation/compose pattern); the Loki and Grafana server images themselves are AGPL-3.0

items.notes: Loki runs in single-binary filesystem mode. Ship logs to it with Promtail/Alloy or the Docker driver; the Loki data source is pre-provisioned in Grafana at http://loki:3100.
items.compose:
# Adapted from Grafana Loki's official docker-compose quickstart pattern
# (https://github.com/grafana/loki/tree/main/production, Apache-2.0 docs), using the official
# loki and grafana images. No bind mounts (named volumes only): a one-shot init container writes
# Loki's config and Grafana's datasource provisioning file into named volumes first.
services:
  loki-config:
    image: docker.io/library/alpine:3.21
    restart: "no"
    volumes:
      - loki-config:/config
    entrypoint:
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        cat > /config/loki-config.yml <<'EOF'
        auth_enabled: false
        server:
          http_listen_port: 3100
        common:
          path_prefix: /loki
          storage:
            filesystem:
              chunks_directory: /loki/chunks
              rules_directory: /loki/rules
          replication_factor: 1
          ring:
            kvstore:
              store: inmemory
        schema_config:
          configs:
            - from: 2024-01-01
              store: tsdb
              object_store: filesystem
              schema: v13
              index:
                prefix: index_
                period: 24h
        limits_config:
          allow_structured_metadata: true
        EOF

  grafana-provisioning:
    image: docker.io/library/alpine:3.21
    restart: "no"
    volumes:
      - grafana-provisioning:/config
    entrypoint:
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        mkdir -p /config/datasources
        cat > /config/datasources/loki.yml <<'EOF'
        apiVersion: 1
        datasources:
          - name: Loki
            type: loki
            access: proxy
            url: http://loki:3100
            isDefault: true
        EOF

  loki:
    image: docker.io/grafana/loki:3.7.8
    depends_on:
      loki-config:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    command: ["-config.file=/etc/loki/loki-config.yml"]
    volumes:
      - loki-config:/etc/loki
      - loki-data:/loki
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${LOKI_PORT}:3100"
    # No healthcheck: grafana/loki's image ships only the loki binary (no shell, wget or curl),
    # so a CMD-SHELL probe can't run inside it. Grafana's own healthcheck (below) is what the
    # "healthy" ready probe waits on; Grafana's datasource proxy will simply retry until Loki
    # answers, which in practice is a couple of seconds after the container starts.

  grafana:
    image: docker.io/grafana/grafana:13.2.2
    depends_on:
      grafana-provisioning:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      loki:
        condition: service_started
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=admin
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - grafana-provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning
      - grafana-data:/var/lib/grafana
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${GRAFANA_PORT}:3000"

volumes:
  loki-config:
  loki-data:
  grafana-provisioning:
  grafana-data:

items.name: Elasticsearch
items.description: Single-node Elasticsearch with security enabled, for local search and indexing experiments.
items.notes: Security is enabled. The built-in `elastic` superuser password is set on first boot from ELASTIC_PASSWORD.
items.compose:
# Adapted from deviantony/docker-elk (MIT) — https://github.com/deviantony/docker-elk
# Single-node variant with security enabled, tuned for local development.
services:
  elasticsearch:
    image: docker.io/library/elasticsearch:8.19.0
    environment:
      - discovery.type=single-node
      - xpack.security.enabled=true
      - ELASTIC_PASSWORD=${ELASTIC_PASSWORD}
      - ES_JAVA_OPTS=-Xms1g -Xmx1g
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${ES_PORT}:9200"
    volumes:
      - es-data:/usr/share/elasticsearch/data
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD-SHELL",
          "curl -s -u elastic:${ELASTIC_PASSWORD} http://localhost:9200/_cluster/health | grep -q '\"status\":\"green\"\\|\"status\":\"yellow\"'"
        ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30

volumes:
  es-data:

items.name: Elasticsearch + Kibana
items.description: Single-node Elasticsearch with security enabled, plus Kibana for browsing and visualizing data.
items.notes: A one-shot setup container sets the kibana_system password via the Elasticsearch security API before Kibana starts, exactly like docker-elk does. Sign in to Kibana with the elastic user.
items.compose:
# Adapted from deviantony/docker-elk (MIT) — https://github.com/deviantony/docker-elk
# The kibana_system password setup step mirrors docker-elk's setup service pattern.
services:
  elasticsearch:
    image: docker.io/library/elasticsearch:8.19.0
    environment:
      - discovery.type=single-node
      - xpack.security.enabled=true
      - ELASTIC_PASSWORD=${ELASTIC_PASSWORD}
      - ES_JAVA_OPTS=-Xms1g -Xmx1g
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${ES_PORT}:9200"
    volumes:
      - es-data:/usr/share/elasticsearch/data
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD-SHELL",
          "curl -s -u elastic:${ELASTIC_PASSWORD} http://localhost:9200/_cluster/health | grep -q '\"status\":\"green\"\\|\"status\":\"yellow\"'"
        ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30

  setup-kibana-user:
    image: docker.io/library/elasticsearch:8.19.0
    depends_on:
      elasticsearch:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: "no"
    entrypoint:
      - bash
      - -c
      - >
        curl -s -u elastic:${ELASTIC_PASSWORD}
        -X POST http://elasticsearch:9200/_security/user/kibana_system/_password
        -H "Content-Type: application/json"
        -d "{\"password\":\"${KIBANA_SYSTEM_PASSWORD}\"}"

  kibana:
    image: docker.io/library/kibana:8.19.0
    depends_on:
      elasticsearch:
        condition: service_healthy
      setup-kibana-user:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    environment:
      - ELASTICSEARCH_HOSTS=http://elasticsearch:9200
      - ELASTICSEARCH_USERNAME=kibana_system
      - ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD=${KIBANA_SYSTEM_PASSWORD}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${KIBANA_PORT}:5601"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -s http://localhost:5601/api/status | grep -q '\"level\":\"available\"'"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30

volumes:
  es-data:

items.name: OpenSearch + Dashboards
items.description: Single-node OpenSearch with the demo security plugin, plus OpenSearch Dashboards for browsing and visualizing data.
items.notes: The OpenSearch API listens on HTTPS with a self-signed demo certificate; browsers and curl need -k / an exception. The admin password must satisfy OpenSearch's strong-password policy (12+ chars, upper/lower/digit/symbol) — the generated password is checked against this.
items.compose:
# Adapted from the official OpenSearch Docker Compose quickstart (Apache-2.0)
# https://github.com/opensearch-project/documentation-website (assets/examples/docker-compose.yml)
# Single-node variant. The default OpenSearch password policy requires a special character;
# it is relaxed to length-only here so the generated alphanumeric password is accepted.
services:
  opensearch:
    image: docker.io/opensearchproject/opensearch:3.8.0
    environment:
      - discovery.type=single-node
      - cluster.name=colima-desktop-opensearch
      - node.name=opensearch
      - bootstrap.memory_lock=true
      - OPENSEARCH_JAVA_OPTS=-Xms1g -Xmx1g
      - OPENSEARCH_INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${OPENSEARCH_PASSWORD}
      - "plugins.security.restapi.password_validation_regex=^.{8,}$$"
      - plugins.security.restapi.password_validation_error_message=Password must be at least 8 characters.
    ulimits:
      memlock:
        soft: -1
        hard: -1
      nofile:
        soft: 65536
        hard: 65536
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${OPENSEARCH_PORT}:9200"
    volumes:
      - opensearch-data:/usr/share/opensearch/data
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD-SHELL",
          "curl -sk -u admin:${OPENSEARCH_PASSWORD} https://localhost:9200/_cluster/health | grep -q '\"status\":\"green\"\\|\"status\":\"yellow\"'"
        ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30

  dashboards:
    image: docker.io/opensearchproject/opensearch-dashboards:3.8.0
    depends_on:
      opensearch:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      - 'OPENSEARCH_HOSTS=["https://opensearch:9200"]'
      - OPENSEARCH_USERNAME=admin
      - OPENSEARCH_PASSWORD=${OPENSEARCH_PASSWORD}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${DASHBOARDS_PORT}:5601"
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD-SHELL",
          "curl -sf -u admin:${OPENSEARCH_PASSWORD} http://localhost:5601/api/status | grep -q '\"state\":\"green\"\\|\"state\":\"yellow\"'"
        ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30

volumes:
  opensearch-data:
